steps.text: The bar only moved a little during the last attempt, which suggests the gripper is contacting it but slipping. I’ll test a straight vertical lift from the handle’s reported contact point, keeping the horizontal position fixed so the grasp does not drift sideways.

steps.text: I found why the close attempts had no effect: `s.move()` stops immediately when the TCP is already at the requested point, so it never sends a gripper command. I’ll send explicit stationary controls to close around the handle, then pull.

o=s.observe(); print('closed',o['tcp'],o['gripper'],o['bodies']['leftpad']['position'],o['bodies']['rightpad']['position'],o['observation'][4:7]); Image.fromarray(s.render()).save('/app/output/grip40.png')
o=s.move([-.0967,.6653,.19],gripper=1,steps=70); print('pull',o['tcp'],o['observation'][4:7],o['goal'],o['bodies']['handle_link']['position'],s.result()); Image.fromarray(s.render()).save('/app/output/grip40_pull.png'); s.save('/app/output/trajectory.npz')
